source.excerpt: The best of artists hath no thought to show / Which the rough stone in its superfluous shell / Doth not include.
trail: The fetched Symonds translation of Michelangelo’s sonnet Non ha l’ottimo artista describes the form within rough stone. It does not contain the supplied prose sentence. The Varchi letter separately describes sculpture by taking away; neither establishes this exact English wording. The actual marble sonnet ↗

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Michelangelo’s sonnet compares a sculptor releasing a form from stone with a lover drawing meaning from a beloved person. The popular prose resembles that artistic image, but it is not the inspected wording of the poem or the related letter on sculpture.
